newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajik govt, Islamists take step towards peace deal.
newsitem.headline: Tajik govt, Islamists take step towards peace deal.

text.p: Tajikistan's government and Islamist opposition took a big step towards a lasting peace settlement on Sunday when they signed a protocol on legalising major political parties, Russian news agencies said.

The agencies said the protocol, a major part of a planned comprehensive peace deal after a four-year civil war, was signed by Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri after two days of difficult talks in Bishkek, capital of neighbouring Kyrgyzstan.

"At last the Tajiks have come to their senses and realised how deadly is further confrontation," Itar-Tass news agency quoted Nuri as saying. Rakhmonov called the document a "major breakthrough", Tass said.

Last December Rakhmonov's secular government and the Islamists agreed a ceasefire to end the civil war, which killed tens of thousands of people in the former Soviet Central Asian State and drove many more from their homes.

Military terms for the peace deal and a power-sharing agreement have been agreed. Legalisation of the opposition was the main outstanding issue in the talks mediated by the United Nations, Russia and Iran.
